{{nihongo|'''Sukuku Shrine'''|須久久神社}} is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Ibaraki, Osaka|ar|إباراكي (أوساكا)|ca|Ibaraki (Osaka)|ce|Ибараки (гӀала)|ceb|Ibaraki (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Ibaraki|eo|Ibaraki (urbo)|es|Ibaraki (Osaka)|et|Ibaraki|fa|ایباراکی، اوساکا|fi|Ibaraki (Osaka)|fr|Ibaraki (Osaka)|ga|Ibaraki|gl|Ibaraki|hy|Իբարակի|it|Ibaraki (Osaka)|ja|茨木市|ka|იბარაკი (ქალაქი)|ko|이바라키시|mzn|ایباراکی، اوساکا|nl|Ibaraki (Osaka)|no|Ibaraki (Osaka)|pl|Ibaraki|pt|Ibaraki (Osaka)|ro|Ibaraki, Osaka|ru|Ибараки (город)|sh|Ibaraki|simple|Ibaraki, Osaka|sr|Ибараки|sv|Ibaraki, Osaka|tg|Ибараки|th|อิบารากิ (จังหวัดโอซากะ)|tl|Ibaraki, Osaka|tr|Ibaraki, Osaka|tt|Ибараки (шәһәр)|uk|Ібаракі (Осака)|ur|ایباراکی، اوساکا|vi|Ibaraki, Ōsaka|war|Ibaraki, Osaka|wuu|茨木市|zh|茨木市|zh_classical|茨木市|zh_min_nan|Ibaraki-chhī|zh_yue|茨木|qid=Q502403}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} of {{ill|Shimashimo district|ja|島下郡|zh|岛下郡|qid=Q10976940}}, {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}}, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}. {{nihongo|'''Sukuku Shrine'''|須久久神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
Currently, the shrine enshrines two deities:
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Kushinadahime|de|Kushinadahime|es|Kushinadahime|fr|Kushinada-hime|it|Kushinadahime|ja|クシナダヒメ|mni|ꯀꯨꯁꯤꯅꯗꯍꯤꯃꯦ|ru|Кусинада-химэ|simple|Kushinadahime|sr|Кушинадахиме|zh|櫛名田比賣|qid=Q505469|lt=Inadahime-no-Mikoto}}

== History ==
According to the “Jingū Zōreishū,” on April 5 of {{ill|Tenpyō|br|Tenpyō|ca|Era Tenpyō|de|Tempyō|es|Tenpyō|fa|تنپیو|fr|Ère Tenpyō|ia|Tenpyo|id|Tempyō|it|Tenpyō|ja|天平|ko|덴표|no|Tenpyō|pt|Tenpyō|ru|Тэмпё|simple|Tenpyō|sr|Тенпјо|tr|Tenpyō|uk|Темпьо (ненґо)|zh|天平 (日本)|zh_yue|天平 (日本)|qid=Q1199879}} 12 (740), the Right Minister {{ill|Ōnakatomi no Kiyomaro|fr|Ōnakatomi no Kiyomaro|ja|大中臣清麻呂|pt|Ōnakatomi no Kiyomaro|qid=Q11431854|lt=Nakatomi Kiyomaro}} secluded himself at this site and enshrined his ancestral deity near his residence. Yukihiko Tembō states that the shrine originally enshrined {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|qid=Q2564508|lt=Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto}}. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} Jinmyōchō, it is recorded as “Sukuku Shrine, two seats, Kuwahazama,” with the other seat being {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Shimizu, Ibaraki, Osaka)|ja|春日神社 (茨木市清水)|zh|春日神社 (茨木市清水)|qid=Q11513674|lt=Kasuga Shrine}}. In ancient times, both sites were part of Shukushō, but in March of {{ill|Meireki|Q1192766|qid=Q1192766}} 1 (1655) they were divided into two villages, and today the name refers only to this shrine.
In Meiji 5 (1872), it was ranked as a village shrine.
